histories.H0: authority never advanced beyond rollback-local state S_old
histories.H1: authority advanced to a newer irreversible effect/state and was then fully restored to the same rollback-local state S_old

address_schemes: SHA derived from deterministic content keyed only by rollback-local logical effect identity
SHA derived from deterministic content including rollback-local generation
SHA derived from an incarnation identifier that is itself stored only in the rollback domain
SHA derived from an incarnation identifier supplied by a rollback-surviving statelessly discoverable witness
object_availability_axes: old object retrievable by recomputed SHA
tested_scope.scope_guard: Mechanism-level indistinguishability result only; no claim about Git object retention duration, production failure rate, or availability semantics.

result.finding: Direct retrieval by a recomputed immutable object SHA changes lookup/discoverability but does not add freshness when the SHA derivation inputs are all rollback-local. H0 and H1 recompute the same address; if the old object is retrievable they receive the same old object, and if it is unavailable they receive the same absence. Retention of a newer object does not help because its address is not derivable from the rolled-back state.

logical_effect_id_reuse.observation: Reusing the same logical effect ID after full rollback reproduces the same deterministic content/address under H0 and H1.
logical_effect_id_reuse.consequence: Content addressing gives integrity/equality for the selected object but cannot tell whether that object is current after an erased advance.

incarnation_scoped_ids.rollback_local_incarnation_source: fails identically because rollback restores the prior incarnation identifier and therefore the prior address
incarnation_scoped_ids.rollback_surviving_incarnation_source: distinguishes the histories, but the safety comes from that nonrollback freshness/incarnation witness, not from direct-by-SHA retrieval itself
incarnation_scoped_ids.minimal_extra_assumption: A rollback-surviving, statelessly discoverable, non-reusable freshness/incarnation value (or equivalent sink-side monotonic lower bound) that is current at the authority decision point.

public_source_status.lookup_result: no results returned in the bounded public-source batch
public_source_status.acceptance_dependency: none; this checkpoint records only the finite mechanism model and does not promote an unverified public implementation claim

observation_vs_inference.observation: All 12 cells whose address inputs are rollback-local map H0 and H1 to the same recomputed address/absence behavior by construction.
observation_vs_inference.inference: Any safe use of deterministic direct-address retrieval after complete rollback requires an additional freshness source outside the rollback-equivalent state; making the address unique with a nonrollback nonce merely relocates the missing witness requirement.

phase1_acceptance.unresolved_child: Find a rollback-surviving statelessly discoverable non-reusable freshness/incarnation witness that itself fits scheduled Chat, zero finite quota, zero incremental cost, and no protected/manual executor.

continuation: Part82: execute exactly one bounded forward-secure/self-certifying-chain leaf. Compare rollback-local forward/back links, mutable current anchors, and a key-evolving or non-reusable incarnation witness under paired histories H0/H1. Test whether any construction lets a future stateless scheduled-Chat invocation detect a fully restored old repository state without relying on a freshness value outside that rollback domain; isolate and reject any construction whose apparent safety is actually supplied by such an external/nonrollback witness.
